concepts.title: Memory as Information Processing: Stages and Stores

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Memory as Information Processing: Stages and Stores' refers to.
questions.a: The information-processing view treats memory as a flow: sensory memory registers input briefly, attention moves it into short-term memory where it survives seconds, and rehearsal encodes it into long-term memory's vast, durable store. Memory has a nature and stages -- encoding, storage and retrieval -- not one box.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Memory as Information Processing: Stages and Stores'.
questions.a: Three doors in sequence -- sensory, short-term, long-term -- and passage depends on attention and rehearsal.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Long-Term Memory: Types and Organisation' refers to.
questions.a: Long-term memory splits into declarative memory -- episodic events and semantic facts that can be stated -- and procedural memory of skills that perform without words. Contents are organised in networks of associations, which is why one cue can unpack a whole episode.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Long-Term Memory: Types and Organisation'.
questions.a: A library with wings -- episodes, facts and skills shelved in linked networks, retrievable by the right cue.

concepts.title: Forgetting, and Strategies for Improving Memory

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Forgetting, and Strategies for Improving Memory' refers to.
questions.a: Forgetting may come from trace decay, interference by older or newer material, or retrieval failure -- the material is present but the cue is missing. Memory can be strengthened by meaningful organisation, elaborative rehearsal, mnemonic devices such as the keyword method, and spaced practice.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Forgetting, and Strategies for Improving Memory'.
questions.a: Forgetting is mislaid, not always erased -- better encoding and cues, spaced over time, keep memory findable.
